item.text:
# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan, 2024: 1B.2 nuclear-rhetoric evidence

Overall read: mildly favorable on restraint, with one important mixed/critical exception. I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Sharif explicitly normalized nuclear use or issued reckless nuclear threats; the clearest support is defensive/self-defense framing, while the strongest contrary item is escalatory India/Pakistan rhetoric at UNGA.

| Valence | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Pakistan's nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-12-24 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism | Sharif said Pakistan’s nuclear program is for peaceful purposes, is for self-defense, and has no aggressive designs. This is direct evidence of restrained nuclear messaging. | 1B.2; also 1B.1 |
| Favorable | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | At UNGA, Sharif urged India to enter dialogue for a peaceful resolution of Kashmir. That is de-escalatory rhetoric, even though it sits alongside sharper claims elsewhere in the same speech. | 1B.2; also 1B.1 |
| Mixed / critical | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | In the same UNGA remarks, Sharif described India’s war doctrine as envisioning “a limited war under the nuclear overhanging” and said Pakistan would respond “most decisively” to Indian aggression. This is not a direct nuclear-use threat, but it is hard-edged brinkmanship-style rhetoric. | 1B.2; also 1B.1 |

## Search gap

- Within the bounded search, I did not find strong 2024 evidence of Sharif himself using apocalyptic nuclear language, threatening first use, or explicitly normalizing nuclear weapons use.
- The evidence I did find is mostly defensive or peace-oriented, with one notable escalatory speech fragment about India and the “nuclear overhanging.”
- On this lens, the best-supported conclusion is that Sharif’s 2024 record was generally restrained on nuclear messaging, but not uniformly so.
